gaps.sentence: It is the first time I ___ paella.
gaps.hint: it is the first time takes present perfect
gaps.explanation: After 'It is the first time', English uses the present perfect: have eaten.

gaps.sentence: I ___ dinner when the lights went out.
gaps.hint: the lights went out interrupted it
gaps.explanation: The lights going out interrupted an ongoing background action, so the past continuous is used: was cooking.

gaps.sentence: When you ___ John tomorrow, please give him my regards.
gaps.hint: no will after when for the future
gaps.explanation: In time clauses referring to the future, English uses the present simple, not 'will': see.

gaps.sentence: I ___ that film three times, and I would happily watch it again.
gaps.hint: life experience counted up to now
gaps.explanation: Experience up to the present with no specific past time takes the present perfect: have seen.

gaps.sentence: When she was a student, she ___ spend her summers hitchhiking around Europe.
gaps.hint: a repeated past action with would
gaps.explanation: 'Would' describes repeated past actions in narrative: would spend.

gaps.sentence: Don't phone between seven and eight — we ___ dinner then.
gaps.hint: in progress at a stated future time
gaps.explanation: Something in progress at a stated future time takes the future continuous: will be having.

gaps.sentence: I can't talk now — I ___ dinner for twelve people.
gaps.hint: now plus a temporary activity in progress
gaps.explanation: 'Now' marks a temporary action in progress, so the present continuous is needed: am cooking.

gaps.sentence: Be quiet! The baby ___ in the next room.
gaps.hint: be quiet means an action in progress
gaps.explanation: The request for quiet shows an action happening at this moment, so use the present continuous: is sleeping.
